# Bug Catalog: `verify/guardian_item_integration.gd`

**Generated by /design-tests on 2026-09-21**
**Scope:** the guardian/item boundary across `game/world.gd`,
`game/item_guardian.gd`, `game/diver.gd`, `game/mini_map.gd`, and
`content/sites.gd`. The public path is a persisted World save, sonar
reveal, a physical guardian `Area3D`, the special-encounter chooser, a
one-diver battle, and key-item reward cleanup.

## What this file does

The planned integration gate protects the deliberate physical-guardian
contract in the release branch: sonar makes a site discoverable, random
encounters do not interrupt while a player is inside that unclaimed site,
and touching its guardian opens the real special-encounter chooser. A win
grants the site key item exactly once and makes that guardian unavailable
both immediately and after saving/reloading. It is also the durable record
for the explicit design decision not to restore raw PR #72's competing
"random encounter inside an invisible revealed circle" acquisition path.

## Public interface

| Symbol | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `ItemGuardian.spots()` | static data API | Returns the two canonical `{item, at, site, look, enemy}` guardian sites. |
| `ItemGuardian.triggered` / `Area3D.body_entered` | signal | Public physical entry point for a guardian site. |
| `World._on_encounter_triggered(d)` | game signal handler | Starts ordinary combat or suppresses the roll in an unclaimed guardian site. |
| `World._on_item_guardian_triggered(...)` | guardian signal handler | Opens the real special chooser and retains a live guardian until result. |
| `World._on_special_encounter_diver_chosen(model)` | chooser signal handler | Starts a one-diver, correct-species special battle. |
| `World._on_battle_finished(result)` | battle signal handler | Awards the item on win, restores special-loss state, and removes a won site. |
| `World._write_save()` / `World._load_save()` | persistence interface | Round-trips claimed/revealed state through the selected save slot. |

## Load-bearing behavior, IO boundaries, and branches

- **Load-bearing comments:** only sonar should make a guardian/site visible;
  guardian sites are deliberate spaces so a random roll cannot disguise the
  artifact fight; loss/cancel leaves the guardian in the world; a win removes
  the guardian and decoy.
- **File-system boundary:** `SaveManager.slot_path(slot)` is read/written by
  the new-game/save/load flow. Tests must backup/restore their disposable
  slot.
- **Time/randomness:** normal encounters are distance/random driven. The
  gate emits the existing public encounter signal instead of relying on a
  probability. Guardian entry and battle-finished signals are likewise driven
  through their normal public paths.
- **Branching points:** active diver vs background diver; unrevealed vs
  revealed vs claimed item; random roll inside vs outside a guardian site;
  cancel/loss/win special result; fresh world vs save reload; Angler shallows
  vs Swordfish trench.

## Bug catalog

| # | Bug (one sentence, failure mode) | Blast radius | Plausibility | Test type | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GI-1 | A claimed key item is loaded after `_build_item_guardians()`, leaving a stale physical guardian that can reappear or retrigger its special fight. | High — progression site can be fought repeatedly after a save/load and the world lies about collected state. | High — guardians are constructed before `_load_save()` assigns `key_items`; current visibility only consulted `revealed_key_items`. | Captured bug / save-load round trip | fixed |
| GI-2 | A random encounter fires inside an unclaimed guardian site, so the player cannot tell whether the fight belongs to exploration pressure or the artifact. | High — repeats the recorded playtest confusion and consumes party resources before the deliberate fight. | Medium — the normal encounter signal is independent of `Area3D` entry. | Decision-table invariant | characterized |
| GI-3 | Sonar revelation, physical entry, and battle species drift apart, so a site shows the wrong enemy or a hidden object grants a reward. | High — breaks discovery, art identity, and key-item progression together. | Medium — site data feeds several runtime systems. | Two-site integration/differential | characterized |
| GI-4 | A special loss/cancel removes the physical guardian, making a real reward permanently missable; or a win leaves it interactable. | High — either blocks progression or permits repeat fights/rewards. | Medium — cleanup has result-sensitive live-node references. | Lifecycle invariant | characterized |

## Test plan

### Bug GI-1 — claimed guardian survives reload

- **Test type:** captured bug / round trip.
- **Description string:**
  > `guardian item integration: claimed item reload has no live guardian — guards against stale post-save guardian fights`
- **What it catches:** Save a world after winning an item, construct/load a
  new World through its real title/load interface, and assert no guardian
  node/site reveal can re-open that claimed reward.
- **Self-critique:**
  - Could this pass for wrong-but-stable output? No. It asserts the externally
    observable post-load world and its public guardian trigger surface.
  - Could this fail under a behavior-preserving refactor? No. It does not
    couple to a helper name or storage representation.

### Bug GI-2 — random-roll ambiguity

- **Test type:** decision-table invariant over both sites.
- **Description string:**
  > `guardian item integration: both unclaimed sites suppress ordinary rolls — guards against artifact/random encounter ambiguity`
- **What it catches:** Emit the normal encounter signal at each site and
  require zero ordinary battle, then emit the physical guardian entry and
  require the chooser.
- **Self-critique:**
  - Could this pass for wrong-but-stable output? No. It observes actual battle
    and prompt state, not a private flag.
  - Could this fail under a behavior-preserving refactor? No. Signal routing
    and displayed result are the game contract.

### Bug GI-3 — site/source drift

- **Test type:** two-site integration/differential.
- **Description string:**
  > `guardian item integration: revealed sites start their mapped one-diver fight — guards against sonar/guardian/species drift`
- **What it catches:** For both canonical site records, reveal it, enter its
  `Area3D`, choose a diver, and assert the special battle uses exactly that
  one site enemy.
- **Self-critique:**
  - Could this pass for wrong-but-stable output? No. The visible/interactive
    path and battle actor identity must agree with the public site record.
  - Could this fail under a behavior-preserving refactor? No. It allows any
    internal node layout and observes only behavior.

### Bug GI-4 — incorrect lifecycle cleanup

- **Test type:** lifecycle invariant.
- **Description string:**
  > `guardian item integration: loss preserves and win retires a site — guards against missable or repeatable key rewards`
- **What it catches:** Lose once and require the same guardian can offer a
  retry; win once and require the key item, guardian, decoy, and site
  presentation retire together before the save/reload case.
- **Self-critique:**
  - Could this pass for wrong-but-stable output? No. It distinguishes all
    externally meaningful battle outcomes.
  - Could this fail under a behavior-preserving refactor? No. It does not
    require a particular implementation of removal.

## Skipped

- Exact sonar particle/minimap pixel layout — visual-only; the focused
  browser evidence validates it at the player surface, while this gate owns
  state/interaction.
- Random encounter probability distribution — already covered by the route
  balance and encounter tuning gates; this slice only establishes the
  deterministic exclusion at a guardian site.
- Raw PR #72's random-circle guardian acquisition — deliberately not pinned:
  it conflicts with the later approved physical Angler/Swordfish artifact
  sites and would reintroduce the ambiguity GI-2 protects against.

## Post-write evaluation

*(Filled in after the high-risk test is written, run red, and the fix is
verified.)*

- **Bugs caught:** GI-1. The first red run showed that a won, saved,
  reloaded `current_pearl` still had a live guardian and could reopen the
  special chooser. The repair retires claimed guardian/decoy/site nodes on
  load and blocks an already-claimed `Area3D` trigger.
- **Bugs characterized:** GI-2, GI-3, and GI-4 across both canonical sites.
- **Bugs discovered during writing:** the saved `revealed_key_items` entry
  also needed to leave the revealed-but-unclaimed state on victory; otherwise
  it could make a retired site visible on a later load.
- **Tests removed:** none.
